clue.text: Wish for departure from France

parts.note: a farewell wish to a traveller, phrased in French: a good-journey greeting borrowed from across the Channel

explanation.walkthrough: 'from France' reads as where the traveller sets off, but it says the wish itself is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase wishing a good journey is the standard farewell said to someone leaving on travels.

clue.text: Publication a major problem?

explanation.walkthrough: The Big Issue is a British street magazine sold by homeless people to earn an income.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Issue is a British magazine sold by homeless vendors, and a big issue is also a serious matter or difficulty.

clue.text: Din made by one in front

indicators.note: the word for one sits inside the word for front, so 'in' places it there

parts.note: the nose is the part of the face at the very front
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A racket kicked up by whoever is leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' gives NOSE, as when someone is said to be 'nosing' ahead; 'made by' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is a loud, unpleasant sound, a racket.

clue.text: Sort of medicine to make you flake out, then recover?

definitions.text: Sort of medicine to make you flake out, then recover?

parts.words: Sort of medicine to make you flake out, then recover?
parts.note: a boxer who flakes out is down for the count; getting up again puts him past that count, a pun on drugs sold without prescription

explanation.walkthrough: In boxing a floored fighter is counted out; recovering means getting up before the count ends. The phrase also names medicine bought without a prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines sold freely in a pharmacy, without a doctor's prescription, are described this way.

clue.text: Commercial jingle, not very good

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, shortened to ad
a jingle is a piece of light verse

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a catchy advertising tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions or results are unfavourable, harmful, the opposite of good.

clue.text: Whereby class see one bit of planet ob-soured?

definitions.text: Whereby class see one bit of planet ob-soured

indicators.note: obscured suggests the letters are muddled and hidden from plain view, so they are rearranged

parts.note: cl. is the standard abbreviation for class
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: a bit of the word planet is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: An astronomy lesson where pupils watch part of a planet being blotted out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: CL, SEE, I and P are shuffled, and the event itself is a heavenly body hiding part of another.
explanation.definitionFit: During this astronomical event one body passes in front of another, hiding part or all of it from view.

clue.text: Non-striker seriously concerned about bowling initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman at the bowler's end worries about the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the non-striker is the batsman not facing the bowler, which makes the surface look like a match report; the definition is a worker who crosses a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike, someone who keeps working while colleagues walk out.

clue.text: American flier hacked ice in pieces

indicators.note: ice broken into pieces is shattered, so the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smashed up some ice in the American way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacked' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'in pieces' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: This small songbird of the tit family lives in North America, so it is an American flier.

clue.text: Inspiration about to occur in course of ablution?

indicators.note: in the course of means in the middle of, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: an ablution is a wash, such as a bath
re is Latin for 'about', concerning

explanation.surface: An idea strikes you while you are washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' suggests a bright idea in the bath; here it is the act of breathing in. 'to occur' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration in the physical sense is drawing air into the lungs, a single intake of it.

clue.text: "Maverick" subtitled in French?

parts.note: imagines a film called Maverick given French subtitles: the caption would carry the French term for an unruly, shocking person

explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase literally means 'terrible child' and is used in English for a provocative maverick.
explanation.definitionFit: This French expression describes an unconventional person who shocks the establishment, a maverick.

clue.text: Smooth passage, if long, penned by French writer

indicators.note: something penned by a writer is enclosed by him, so the long-sign goes inside the writer's name

parts.note: André Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate
L is the abbreviation for long, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A French author writes a long, flowing piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' looks like authorship, but it is a container: L inside GIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A glide is a smooth, effortless movement through the air or over a surface.

clue.text: Fourteenth card forming part of suit?

definitions.text: Fourteenth card forming part of suit?

parts.words: Fourteenth card forming part of suit?
parts.note: a pack's suits run to thirteen cards, so a fourteenth looks impossible; but suit here is courtship, and the card is sent on 14 February

explanation.walkthrough: Card suits have thirteen cards each, which kills the card-game reading; 'suit' is wooing, and the card is sent on February 14th.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting card sent to a sweetheart on 14 February is part of courting someone.

clue.text: bottom, adorned with royal insignia

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'bottom, adorned with royal insignia (7)': the opening words, including the definition (and the W wordplay piece of S(W)EAT+ER), are cut off; no search found the full clue.

clue.text: Slit left in carton

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the carton word, as 'in' instructs

parts.note: a carton is a packet

explanation.surface: A gap has been left in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A placket is an opening or slit in a garment, such as at the top of a skirt, for fastening.

clue.text: Centre ended up vandalised-it's without parallel

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed about, so these three words' letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A town centre was trashed in a way nobody had seen before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never done or known before has no earlier example to compare with, no parallel.

clue.text: Unrealistic aspiration by one in degree course -minimally difficult paper

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the degree, as 'in' instructs

parts.note: PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is a degree course, famously at Oxford
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: minimally means taking the least possible part of the word, its opening letter

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A hopeless ambition for a student with a hard exam.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE is a British university degree in Philosophy, Politics and Economics; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasy or hope that will never be realised, like an opium smoker's vision, is a wild, impractical ambition.

clue.text: Outlined method of treating the decks

indicators.note: a method of treating something works it over, so the letters of the two words are reorganised

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to clean a ship's decks were given in brief.
explanation.definitionFit: To sketch is to draw roughly or describe in outline, giving the main features only.

clue.text: Walk on water?

parts.note: a walk taken aboard a ship at sea, rather than a miracle; the stretch of upper deck where passengers stroll

explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk on water' suggests a miracle; it is a stroll on a liner's upper deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner's upper deck where passengers stroll is a walkway that sits out at sea.

clue.text: Poem English class go over, extremely unreadable

parts.note: cl. is the standard abbreviation for class

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word go is turned back to front
extremely means taking the extreme ends, first and last letters, of the word

explanation.surface: A literature class finds a poem impossible to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go over' turns GO into OG; 'extremely unreadable' gives U and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pastoral poem, often a dialogue between shepherds, as written by Virgil.

clue.text: Relief mission, look, supported by doctor with small surgery?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first word sits on top of the following ones, which hold it up

parts.note: an air is a look or manner, as in 'an air of confidence'
op is the short form of operation, a surgery

explanation.surface: A doctor carries out minor operations during an aid mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies dropped from an aircraft to people cut off by disaster are a common form of aid delivery.

clue.text: Clown performing in silk overall?

parts.note: Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown in Britain
a performer is on, on stage

explanation.surface: A clown does his act dressed in a silk jumpsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown (Nicolai Poliakoff) was Britain's best-known circus clown; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A silkworm spins a casing of silk thread around itself, a covering for its whole body.

clue.text: Nun's first to wear gold ring? Second or third, maybe

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: what is worn sits around the wearer, so the gold ring encloses the nun's letter

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word for nun

explanation.surface: A nun puts on a gold ring for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers like second and third that give position in a sequence are examples of this kind of number.

clue.text: One engaged in barter after ordering food

indicators.note: one being engaged in something is taken up inside it, so the letter goes within
after being ordered the letters of barter are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone haggles for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after ordering' turns BARTER into RAREBT, and I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a dish of melted cheese on toast.

clue.text: Mistakes often concealed by supporters?

explanation.definitionFit: A boob is a blunder, and in slang breasts are often hidden by bras, which give support.

clue.text: Longing to be asked to bowl?

definitions.text: Longing to be asked to bowl?

parts.words: Longing to be asked to bowl?
parts.note: in cricket a bowler delivers an over, so a bowler keen to be given one is keen for an over

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls from one bowler, so someone eager for one wants to bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Being too keen, impatient to the point of excess, describes someone desperate to be picked.

clue.text: Soup with bread in German hospital

parts.note: Brot is the German word for bread
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A German hospital serves soup and bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is a thin soup of stock with meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Call American in New England

indicators.note: the American abbreviation goes inside that for New England

explanation.surface: Phoning an American who lives in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: To call a person something is to give them a title or label.

clue.text: Described as "squeezed out"

explanation.definitionFit: Ideas put into words are stated, and juice pressed from fruit is forced out.
